title: The I ♥ NY logo
hook: One of the most copied logos in the world was sketched in a taxi and given away free.
peek: In 1977 Milton Glaser sketched I ♥ NY for a New York State tourism campaign, reportedly in the back of a taxi. He did the work for free. His original sketch is now in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art.
lede: In 1977, New York State hired an advertising agency to promote tourism at a time when the state, and New York City especially, badly needed good news. The designer Milton Glaser agreed to help without a fee. The story goes that he scribbled the idea in red crayon on a scrap of paper in the back of a taxi. That rough sketch is now in the Museum of Modern Art.

bullets.text: The design is a rebus: you read the red heart as the word 'love'. Glaser stacked the I and the heart over N and Y so the whole thing works as a compact square.
The logo lettering is set in American Typewriter, a rounded slab-serif face. Its friendly, slightly old-fashioned shapes soften the bold red heart.
Because Glaser gave the design away, it belongs to New York State, which holds the trademark and licenses it. It has appeared on countless mugs, T-shirts and bags.
The idea proved easy to borrow. Cities, towns and shops around the world have copied the heart-in-the-middle formula, which is one reason the original is among the most imitated logos ever made.
